# Kits — packaged uses of the memory system

*Draft, 2026-09-07. Generated by Claude from a design conversation with Matt; wording to be revised in his voice. Decisions marked **decided** are Matt's; everything else is a proposal.*

## The problem this solves

The memory graph is the core of Zynkbot and, to a new user, the least legible part of it. People see a graph and ask what it is for. A kit is a packaged, opt-in use of the memory system that answers that question with a job anyone recognises. The first one is the kitchen.

## What a kit is

A kit is data, not code. Four parts, shipped as one JSON file:

| Part | What it is | Example (Kitchen kit) |
|---|---|---|
| Standing instructions | A short block injected into the system prompt while the kit is on; the standing-instructions memory tier from `labs/` is the carrier | "The user is tracking what they cook and eat. When they describe a meal, store it as a memory with the date, the dish, and any quantities they state (carbs, calories). When they ask what to cook, prefer dishes they have liked and avoid ingredients they have refused. Keep answers short." |
| Namespace | A memory category the kit writes into, so its memories can be shown, exported or deleted together | `kitchen` |
| Opening questions | Asked once when the kit is switched on; answers become the first memories | "Are you following a way of eating right now (keto, vegetarian, none)?", "Foods you will not eat?", "Any allergies?", "How many people do you usually cook for?" |
| Quick prompts | Two or three chips above the message box while the kit is on | "What can I make tonight?", "Log what I just ate", "How am I doing this week?" |

Optional fifth part: a report section, used by the "what do you know about me" memory report when it exists ("Kitchen: 14 meals logged, 3 recipes liked, carbs this week…").

A kit has no permissions, no network access and no code path of its own. Everything it does, the user could do by typing. That is deliberate: kits inherit the memory system's promise (local, visible, editable, deletable) without adding a trust surface.

## How a user opts in

- **End of onboarding:** one card. "Want to try Zynkbot in the kitchen? It will remember what you cook and what you like, and help you plan meals. Everything stays on this device." Buttons: *Turn on* / *Skip*. Skip is the default and nothing is created.
- **System Controls panel:** a **Kits** section between Snap-ins and Knowledge Base (**decided**). It lists every kit with a switch. Kits that do not exist yet are shown greyed with a "future" tag so the shape of the idea is visible from day one: Kitchen (on/off), Garden (future), Workouts (future), Reading (future), Household (future). The greyed rows are labels only; nothing behind them.
- **Turning a kit off** removes its instructions and chips immediately. Its memories stay unless the user presses *Forget everything from this kit*, which deletes the namespace.

### "Make it forget and start again"

The line for the kitchen: *if you fall off your diet, you never have to feel guilty. Tell Zynkbot to forget it ever happened and start again when you are ready.* True today on one device because a kit's memories live in their own namespace. Two conditions before it is said to paying users:
1. Deletions must propagate across devices — the ZynkSync outbox refactor (tombstones), KI-028.
2. A cloud backup keeps the old memories until the next backup overwrites it; "forget" should trigger a fresh backup or say so.

## Pricing tiers (decided by Matt, 2026-09-07)

| Tier | Model | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Zynkbot core | Free, complete | Includes the Kitchen kit |
| Other kits | One-time purchase each | Deliberately not a subscription: nobody should pay monthly to cook in their own kitchen |
| Professional snap-ins | Monthly subscription | The snap-in platform (`labs/snapin_platform/`) |
| Modes and enterprise | Above that | Parenting / Elder modes, organisational deployments |

Zero-trust is unchanged: a kit never routes anything through ContainAI; purchase is the only interaction.

## Selling kits without a store in the app

**Proposal:** the app shows the catalogue (name, description, price, "available at zynkbot.com"); the purchase happens on the website; the buyer receives a small signed licence file (or a code) and drops it into the app, which verifies the signature offline and unlocks the kit. No account, no server call from the app, consistent with the rest of the product.

**Google Play constraint, stated plainly.** Play's rules require digital goods bought inside an app distributed on Play to go through Google Play Billing, and historically forbade steering users to an outside payment. A US court order in *Epic v. Google* (injunction in force from late 2025, upheld on appeal in 2025) requires Google to permit links to outside purchases in the US for a period, and Google has published conditions and fees for that. The situation is live and must be re-checked at the moment of Play submission. Safe design regardless:
- The desktop builds show the full catalogue with buy links.
- The Android build shows the catalogue and the "enter licence" screen; whether it shows a buy link depends on the policy in force when it ships. Worst case, Android says "available at zynkbot.com" with no link, which Play has always allowed for content the user obtains elsewhere.
- The beta (closed testing track) is unaffected; nothing is for sale in it.

## What the mechanism needs from the code

1. Standing-instructions tier: inject a kit's instruction block into the system prompt while the kit is on (`conversation_engine.rs::build_prompt`). The block is per-kit, short, and shown to the user in the Kits section so nothing is hidden.
2. Namespace on write: memories extracted while a kit is on are tagged with the kit's namespace when the model says the fact belongs to it (the MEMORY_EXTRACT line gains an optional namespace hint).
3. Opening questions: a small dialog; answers stored through the normal "Remember:" path with the kit namespace.
4. Quick prompts: chips above the input, from the kit JSON.
5. Kits section in System Controls; onboarding card; "forget this kit" (delete-by-namespace, which exists in the Memory Manager code path).
6. Event dates on memories (from the 2026-09-07 analyst pass): "what did I eat yesterday" and "this week" need when-it-happened, not when-it-was-said.
7. Quantities kept as numbers when stated ("32 g carbs") so a weekly total is a sum, not a guess — a small structured field on the memory, optional.

Estimate: two days for 1–5 with the Kitchen kit; 6–7 are shared with the memory report.

## The Kitchen kit, in full

```json
{
  "id": "kitchen",
  "name": "Kitchen",
  "version": 1,
  "tagline": "Remembers what you cook and what you like. Helps you plan the next meal.",
  "namespace": "kitchen",
  "instructions": "The user is using Zynkbot to plan and track what they cook and eat. When they describe a meal or a recipe, store it as a memory with today's date, the dish, how it turned out, and any quantities they state (for example carbohydrates, calories, servings). When they ask what to cook, suggest dishes that fit any way of eating they have told you about, prefer what they have liked, avoid ingredients they have refused or are allergic to, and say why you chose it in one line. When they ask how they are doing, summarise the current week from their logged meals in plain words. Never invent a meal they did not mention. Keep answers short; they are cooking.",
  "questions": [
    { "id": "diet", "text": "Are you following a way of eating right now? (keto, low-carb, vegetarian, none, something else)" },
    { "id": "refuse", "text": "Any foods you just won't eat?" },
    { "id": "allergies", "text": "Any allergies or intolerances?" },
    { "id": "household", "text": "How many people do you usually cook for?" }
  ],
  "prompts": [
    { "label": "What can I make tonight?", "text": "What can I make tonight from what I usually have, that fits how I'm eating?" },
    { "label": "Log what I just ate", "text": "Remember: I just ate " },
    { "label": "How am I doing this week?", "text": "How am I doing this week against how I said I want to eat?" }
  ],
  "report": { "title": "Kitchen", "fields": ["meals logged", "recipes liked", "recipes to avoid", "weekly quantities"] }
}
```

## Tester task (for the beta package)

"For two weeks, tell Zynkbot what you cooked and how it went, by voice or typed, in whatever words you like. Once or twice, ask it what to make. At the end, open Memory Manager and look at the Kitchen memories. Tell us: did it remember the right things, did it suggest anything you actually cooked, and did anything it remembered make you uncomfortable?"

## Open questions

- Should a kit be allowed to set a containment mode (for example a child-safe kit)? Proposal: no; modes stay separate.
- Kit versioning and updates for purchased kits (a signed file with a version; the app keeps the newer).
- Whether third parties can publish kits (later, through the snap-in platform's signing scheme).
